content.text: Eid al-Fitr is one of two major holidays on the Islamic calendar. It’s an Arabic term meaning “Festival of Breaking Fast,” because it’s celebrated at the end of Ramadan. Eid is the Arabic word for “festival” and is often celebrated with prayer, food, new clothes, gifts, and visiting relatives throughout the three-day holiday.When is Ramadan, and how is it observed?Ramadan follows the lunar calendar and the dates shift slightly each year. This year, 2026, Ramadan began on the night of February 17 and ends tonight, March 19. Ramadan begins when the moon is sighted and ends after 29-30 days on a holiday called Eid. The most well-known element of Ramadan is fasting from dawn to dusk for all healthy adult Muslims. This means Muslims do not eat or drink (no, not even water!) during daylight hours. At sunset, the daily fast ends, and the evening meal begins. People frequently have large gatherings to break the fast and enjoy a meal called an iftar, sharing the occasion with friends and family. It is also encouraged to do extra acts of worship and prayer during Ramadan.Muslims live and practice in cultures around the world, so there is a wide variety of foods and traditions that can be part of each person’s observance of Ramadan. In general, Muslims are encouraged to be the best version of themselves during this month, to fast, give in charity, increase prayer and practice self-control.Learn more about Ramadan and Eid al-Fitr:
